lines: This is Tare.
The label is not the delivery.
AI agents now pay for data on their own, over x402.
The seller describes the delivery: twelve hundred and forty unique records, no nulls.
The agent pays, and moves on.
Spending caps limit how much it can pay. Nothing checks what came back.
Tare is an independent check of what a seller delivered.
Before paying, it reads the seller's own advertisement.
After delivery, SERV Reasoning reads the seller's promise,
and plain code counts what actually arrived.
Here is the Tare console. Every payment is real x402 on Kite testnet, settled by Pieverse.
Seller A promised twelve hundred and forty unique records, with no nulls.
Code counted eight hundred and sixty unique, and forty empty timestamps.
Its advertisement also promised a score field. It never arrived.
Dispute. Here is the real settlement hash, and seller A is now held.
Buy from seller A again, and Tare stops before any payment. The payment counter does not move.
Seller B promised two hundred records, and delivered two hundred. Verified.
Every receipt keeps both promises word for word, next to what code measured.
The settlement hash, the body hash and the prompt hash let anyone repeat the check.
Tare publishes signed seller records.
Another agent that trusts the feed is warned, and never pays seller A.
And anyone can check a seller before paying.
SERV reads. Code decides. The wallet pays.
Spending policies decide whether to pay. Tare checks what you got.
